findings.reason: a node implementing §3 as written ships a rule that misses the phrase the plan itself names as evidence, so its done-when ("each new spelling") passes while the rule still fails on the corpus it exists to police; the plan needs "go"/"goes" in the onward-noun verb set and an allowing window between the qualifier and its noun.
findings.text: §3 grants the onward-noun forms ("follow-up", "later", "next" or "separate" node, section or plan) only to "sent to or going to", while binding "go"/"goes" to "§N" alone, so "the remaining non-blocking items go to a follow-up node" — the example §1 quotes from power_convertor/docs/briefs/prose-follow-on-audit.md:11 — is not matched, and neither is live plan prose carrying the same shape at power_convertor/docs/plans/filter-recommendation-for-coil-health.html:226 ("go to a follow-up figure node") or power_convertor/docs/plans/quench-detection-converter-pickup.html:84 ("go to a separate plan"); the adjective-to-noun window is also fixed at one word, so "a follow-up figure node" would escape even a "going to a follow-up node" form

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every reckon anchor resolves at head 98c62ac0f: _render_document summary at 404-407 and plan-verdict at 417, _landed_record_shell at 1184 delegating at 1194, the shell created by _apply_evidence_appends at 1263, _evidence_record_path at 1172, _apply_evidence_appends at 1230, _section_key at 50, the available set at 349, _prose_deferred_work_term at 993, _DEFERRED_WORK_TERM at 419, _require_authored_value at _store_section_ops.py:153, the followup add at mcp_edit_plan.py:257, and synthesize_evidence at project_maintenance_commands.py:1473; the plan's external power_convertor census was re-measured in that checkout and reproduces exactly (follow-on(s) 501 across 19 plans, 76 in shared-coil-supply-model; next node 9; followon 5; later node 2; separate node 2; deferred to 1; carry/carried to §N 6 combined), and the brief line §1 quotes is at power_convertor/docs/briefs/prose-follow-on-audit.md:11.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each implementable section states a falsifiable measure with named negative controls (three in §2, five in §3, seven in §4), and each control is a change to the mechanism that must turn the stated assertion red; §3's enumeration of spellings is the subject of the reasoning finding below.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log is required under the run directory with its revision and literal command on the first line and a bare EXIT= on the last, which is a durable path, and no log is placed in a node-local or scratch location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the three new test filenames and every proposed symbol (_evidence_record_path relocation, lost_anchors, data-evidence-origin) are named by what they do, with no plan labels, stage ids, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1's root cause matches its evidence and I reproduced it (_render_document over an empty record set emits "0 committed run(s), 0 section-anchored comment(s), and 0 landed commit(s)" and plan-verdict "qualified", and synthesize_landed_record refuses at 665-670 when the ledger is empty, so the shell at 1184/1263 is the only zero source), and §2's and §4's mechanisms run on the named production callers (_apply_evidence_appends, synthesize_landed_record, the audit's deferred_work_term over the whole plan document including the r-fu-outcome prose that _apply_resolve writes); but §3's enumerated spelling forms do not cover the very example §1 cites.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 is one deliverable (an append-created record claims no counts), §3 is one rule read at every write site, and §4's mark, carry-forward, refusal and lost_anchors are the preventive and detective halves of one retention guarantee, not two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-section-depends-on declares s3 on s2 and s4 on s2 and s3, which matches the shared reckon/_store.py writes each section performs, and plan-after "a-finished-plan-closes" resolves to docs/plans/a-finished-plan-closes.html.
